questions.prompt: Why is memory acquisition fundamentally different from disk acquisition in terms of forensic soundness?
options: Memory acquisition is always faster than disk acquisition
Acquiring RAM necessarily runs a program inside the exact memory being captured, meaning there's no way to avoid touching the evidence to collect it
Memory acquisition never requires hashing the resulting image
Disk acquisition is more volatile than memory acquisition
questions.explanation: Unlike a disk image, capturing RAM requires an acquisition tool to run inside the very memory being captured -- some footprint is unavoidable, so soundness is about minimizing and documenting it, not eliminating it.

questions.prompt: What can hiberfil.sys and a crash dump (MEMORY.DMP) provide when a live memory capture wasn't taken?
options: Nothing useful -- only live captures are analyzable
A memory snapshot from a past point in time, analyzable with the same tools and plugins as a live capture
A complete replacement for live acquisition with no limitations
Only network connection data, not process information
questions.explanation: Both are cold sources reflecting memory state from some point in the past rather than the moment response began, but both are directly analyzable with Volatility and other memory forensics tools.

questions.prompt: Why might a hypervisor-side VM snapshot be preferable to an in-guest acquisition tool in some cases?
options: VM snapshots are always faster to acquire
It never touches the guest OS at all, which matters if the guest is suspected of running anti-forensic tooling that could detect and interfere with an in-guest capture
In-guest acquisition tools are illegal to use
questions.explanation: A snapshot taken from the hypervisor side never runs anything inside the guest OS, so a guest running anti-forensic or anti-debugging code never sees the capture happen at all.

questions.prompt: An acquired memory image is significantly smaller than the system's installed RAM. What does this most likely indicate?
options: This is completely normal and expected
A partial or failed capture, not simply a small memory footprint
The system has excellent memory compression
The acquisition tool used too much memory itself
questions.explanation: A significant size mismatch between the captured image and installed RAM is a strong sign that the acquisition didn't complete successfully, and should be treated as a red flag in the acquisition process itself.
